subject: Granite Nexus renewal — concession package & term-reset approval needed
messages:
From: Elliott Shaw <elliott.shaw@granitenexus.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace Lim <grace.lim@granitenexus.com>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal posture from Granite Nexus – urgent

Avery,

Appreciate your help so far. We’re at an internal decision point — procurement is pushing for a lower committed spend or they pull the workload to a major cloud-managed provider. The product team has been happy with Redwood latency, but finance is focused on unit economics.

Short summary of ask from our side:
- 20% first-year discount or a one-time credit to cover migration costs
- Reset term to 12 months with monthly true-ups (we're on an annual prepay today)
- SLA overlay covering <100ms p95 for the most critical model route, or a partial credit if not met

If you can put together a tangible concession package and executive note we can share with leadership, we’ll fast-track a signoff.

Thanks,
Elliott Shaw
Head of Product
Granite Nexus

(Attachment referenced: GN_internal_rationale.pdf)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Elliott Shaw <elliott.shaw@granitenexus.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 May 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal posture from Granite Nexus – urgent

Elliott —

Thanks for the clear summary. I’m pulling together options for the Deal Desk and will propose a scoped concession set that balances cost impact and retention risk. Quick clarifications to ensure we give you something executable:
- Is the request for a 20% across-the-board on hosted API usage, or specifically on the reserved capacity line items?
- For the SLA overlay, is the 100ms p95 requirement limited to the 3 inference routes listed in appendix A?

Proposed immediate next step: I’ll escalate to my manager (Marissa) and our revenue ops lead (Vivek) with a recommended package and ask for executive approval for a one-time migration credit + a temporary term reset. I’ll include quantification of ARR impact and a mitigation plan (cloud burst fallback, usage caps). Can you confirm you want the reset to 12 months with monthly true-ups? Once confirmed, I’ll submit the formal approval request.

—Avery
Avery Johnson
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Attachment: draft_MA_outline.txt (stub)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 May 2028 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Renewal posture from Granite Nexus – urgent

Looping in Vivek for executive authority but please include Finance impact calc (Ben) and the operational feasibility statement (SRE/Platform) before we finalize. Initial read: this is a strategic account with ~$1.2M ARR; losing them creates compounding revenue and reputational risk. We should evaluate a blended concession: smaller % discount + migration credit + SLA guardrail for a limited period.

Ben — can you run a 12-month P&L hit for the following two options and attach to the approval packet:
A) 15% discount on reserved capacity + $75k one-time migration credit + SLA credits capped at $50k
B) 8% discount + $150k migration credit + 3-month SLA overlay guarantee (monitoring/ops commitment)

Aim for numbers by EOD Monday. I’ll draft the exec note once we have the quant.

Marissa Cole
Head of Enterprise Sales — West, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Renewal posture from Granite Nexus – urgent

Marissa / Avery —

Attached the breakouts you requested. High level: Option A = estimated ARR hit $180k first year, Option B = $140k first year but higher cash outlay now. I included sensitivity rows for usage variance ±25%. Key caveat: the migration credit will be paid on invoice as a one-time credit against their next renewal invoice. SLA credit modeled as up to 6% of monthly bill, capped at $50k across the term (we propose that cap).

Also flagged operational risk with a 100ms p95 target — our current production baseline for that route is ~110–120ms under typical load. Delivering 100ms p95 reliably would require prioritization on their pool (dedicated hot lanes) or a limited model variant (quantized) which would slightly change output characteristics. SRE estimates a configuration and testing window of ~3 weeks to validate.

Files attached: GN_cost_breakdown_Q3.xlsx, impact_sensitivity.csv

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations Analyst, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 May 2028 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive approval: Granite Nexus – concession package

Team —

Thanks for the fast triage. I’ve reviewed Ben’s financials and the risk profile. Given Granite Nexus’ strategic footprint and the narrow window before procurement issues freeze the deal, I approve the following controlled concession package for signoff: 

- 12-month term reset with monthly true-ups (effective at renewal date)
- One-time migration credit of $125,000 applied on next invoice
- 10% discount on reserved capacity for first 12 months only
- SLA overlay: committed 100ms p95 for the three critical routes; SLA credits to be paid per our standard SLA schedule, capped at $50,000 total

Conditions:
1) Customer must sign the revised SOW and a 30-day remediation SLA addendum (I’ve attached the DocuSign link to the approval package).
2) SRE to prioritize a validation run and confirm telemetry within 3 weeks; if 100ms p95 is not met after validation, we revert to a mitigation plan (performance tiering) with proportional credits.
3) Legal to confirm the term-reset language is limited to the quoted SOW and does not change standard renewal policy globally.

Marissa — please prepare the executive note for Elliott and route to Legal/Contracts for final redline. Avery — coordinate the DocuSign envelope and confirm the customer acceptance window. Ben — update the forecast; mark $125k credit as a one-time contra.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: granite_nexus_exec_note_v1.docx, DocuSign envelope ID: 0A1B2C3D4E
